8a5e255d-8320-42aa-acf4-f67f8c308894.name: 2-Minute Relaxation
8a5e255d-8320-42aa-acf4-f67f8c308894.description: Quick relaxation technique for instant stress relief.
8a5e255d-8320-42aa-acf4-f67f8c308894.history: Simple technique combining breathing and progressive relaxation principles.
8a5e255d-8320-42aa-acf4-f67f8c308894.safety_warning: If you feel dizzy, lightheaded, or short of breath, stop and return to normal breathing. Avoid breath holds if you are pregnant or have uncontrolled high blood pressure, heart rhythm problems, or a history of fainting; consult a clinician if unsure.

instructions.instruction: Stop what you're doing. Close your eyes.
Take a deep breath in for 4 seconds.
Hold for 2 seconds.
Exhale slowly for 6 seconds while relaxing shoulders.
Repeat 4-5 times.
Open eyes slowly, feeling calmer.

3a5cbbd8-3e91-49db-a082-0362bee11168.name: 4-7-8 Breathing
3a5cbbd8-3e91-49db-a082-0362bee11168.description: Promotes relaxation and helps with falling asleep faster. Also known as the relaxing breath.
3a5cbbd8-3e91-49db-a082-0362bee11168.history: Developed by Dr. Andrew Weil based on pranayama techniques.
3a5cbbd8-3e91-49db-a082-0362bee11168.safety_warning: If you feel dizzy, return to normal breathing.

instructions.instruction: Place the tip of your tongue against the ridge behind your upper front teeth.
Exhale completely through your mouth, making a whoosh sound.
Inhale quietly through your nose for 4 seconds.
Hold your breath for 7 seconds.
Exhale completely through your mouth for 8 seconds.
Repeat the cycle 3-4 times.

a9e16563-e95e-4297-adfe-34134fa2c2a6.name: Alternate Nostril Breathing
a9e16563-e95e-4297-adfe-34134fa2c2a6.description: Balances the left and right hemispheres of the brain. A yogic practice for mental clarity.
a9e16563-e95e-4297-adfe-34134fa2c2a6.history: Ancient pranayama technique from Yoga tradition (~3000 BCE).
a9e16563-e95e-4297-adfe-34134fa2c2a6.safety_warning: Avoid if you have a cold or nasal congestion.

instructions.instruction: Sit comfortably with your spine straight.
Use your right thumb to close your right nostril.
Inhale slowly through your left nostril.
Close your left nostril with your ring finger.
Open your right nostril and exhale slowly.
Inhale through the right nostril.
Close right nostril, open left, and exhale.
This completes one cycle. Repeat for the session duration.

tips: Balances left and right brain hemispheres
Great for focus and calming anxiety

52d10895-2cad-4723-a713-099f63a334ab.name: Anapanasati
52d10895-2cad-4723-a713-099f63a334ab.description: Thai Buddhist mindfulness of breathing. Direct from Buddha's teachings.
52d10895-2cad-4723-a713-099f63a334ab.history: Anapanasati is the Buddha's core meditation teaching, preserved in Thai forest tradition. "Ana" means inhale, "apana" means exhale, "sati" means mindfulness.
52d10895-2cad-4723-a713-099f63a334ab.safety_warning: If focusing on the breath increases anxiety, panic symptoms, or dizziness, stop and shift attention to external sounds or open your eyes. Practice in a safe seated position; consult a clinician if you have a trauma history and breath-focused practice is triggering.

instructions.instruction: Sit in a stable, comfortable meditation posture.
Close eyes and bring attention to natural breathing.
Simply observe breath at the nostrils or belly.
When mind wanders, gently return to breath.
No need to control breath - just observe its natural rhythm.
Continue for 20-45 minutes, deepening concentration.

340bfa7c-c42c-4071-aeb8-1533d47383e4.name: Berserker Breath
340bfa7c-c42c-4071-aeb8-1533d47383e4.description: Norse warrior breathing for courage and fearlessness. Controlled intensity.
340bfa7c-c42c-4071-aeb8-1533d47383e4.history: Inspired by Norse Berserker warriors who used breath and meditation to enter altered states of consciousness before battle.
340bfa7c-c42c-4071-aeb8-1533d47383e4.safety_warning: Very intense practice. Not for heart conditions or high blood pressure. Do not drive after.

instructions.instruction: Stand in a strong warrior stance.
Take 20 rapid, powerful breaths through nose.
Each breath should be forceful but controlled.
On the last exhale, let out a primal roar or growl.
Inhale deeply and hold for as long as possible.
Exhale and return to calm. Feel powerful but centered.

53efdc88-1fc3-48f2-8c3d-01a765b97ae3.name: Bhastrika
53efdc88-1fc3-48f2-8c3d-01a765b97ae3.description: Bellows Breath. A powerful energizing technique using rapid forceful inhales and exhales.
53efdc88-1fc3-48f2-8c3d-01a765b97ae3.history: Bellows breath from ancient Yoga tradition for energy.
53efdc88-1fc3-48f2-8c3d-01a765b97ae3.safety_warning: Avoid if pregnant, have high blood pressure, heart disease, or during menstruation. Stop if dizzy.

instructions.instruction: Sit comfortably with spine straight.
Take a deep breath in and exhale completely.
Begin rapid, forceful breathing through both nostrils.
Both inhale and exhale are active and equal in force.
Do 20-30 breaths, then take a deep breath and hold briefly.
Exhale slowly. Rest and repeat 2-3 rounds.

tips: Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable

1f551efa-967d-4620-9637-1046c1cbc286.name: Bhramari
1f551efa-967d-4620-9637-1046c1cbc286.description: Bee Breath. The humming vibration calms the mind and activates the vagus nerve deeply.
1f551efa-967d-4620-9637-1046c1cbc286.history: Bhramari pranayama (bee breath) from Yoga tradition.
1f551efa-967d-4620-9637-1046c1cbc286.safety_warning: Hum gently—do not strain or force the exhale. Stop if you feel dizzy, pressure/pain in the ears, or worsening tinnitus. Avoid pressing on the ears if you have an ear infection, recent ear surgery, or significant ear pain; consult a clinician if unsure.

instructions.instruction: Sit comfortably and close your eyes.
Place your index fingers gently on the cartilage of your ears.
Take a deep breath in through your nose.
As you exhale, make a humming sound like a bee (mmmmm).
Feel the vibration in your head, face, and chest.
Continue for 5-10 rounds, breathing naturally between hums.

tips: The vibration directly stimulates your vagus nerve
Great for anxiety and before sleep

a99e5344-425e-4c3d-81e2-6736bd051c55.name: Box Breathing
a99e5344-425e-4c3d-81e2-6736bd051c55.description: A simple technique to calm your nervous system and reduce stress. Used by Navy SEALs for focus and calm.
a99e5344-425e-4c3d-81e2-6736bd051c55.history: Used by Navy SEALs for stress control in high-pressure situations.

instructions.instruction: Sit comfortably with your back straight and feet flat on the floor.
Inhale slowly through your nose for 4 seconds.
Hold your breath for 4 seconds.
Exhale slowly through your mouth for 4 seconds.
Hold your breath for 4 seconds.
Repeat the cycle for the duration of the session.

tips: Used by Navy SEALs for stress control
Keep equal timing for all 4 phases
Focus on the corners of the "box"

e78f8b20-d857-4b95-8e72-b1ea2409cce1.name: Breath of Fire
e78f8b20-d857-4b95-8e72-b1ea2409cce1.description: Kundalini breathing technique with rapid, rhythmic breaths powered by the diaphragm.
e78f8b20-d857-4b95-8e72-b1ea2409cce1.history: Ancient Kundalini Yoga technique to awaken energy and cleanse the body.
e78f8b20-d857-4b95-8e72-b1ea2409cce1.safety_warning: Avoid during pregnancy, menstruation, high blood pressure. Stop if dizzy or lightheaded.

instructions.instruction: Sit with spine straight, hands on knees.
Take a deep breath to prepare.
Begin rapid, equal inhales and exhales through the nose.
Pump your belly: pull in on exhale, release on inhale.
Keep chest relatively still, breath comes from diaphragm.
Start with 1 minute, rest, then repeat.

900c82e8-9a30-493c-895e-a9375263c9ab.name: Burst Breathing
900c82e8-9a30-493c-895e-a9375263c9ab.description: Short, sharp breaths to energize and reset the nervous system. From Russian Systema.
900c82e8-9a30-493c-895e-a9375263c9ab.history: Systema combat breathing technique for instant energy and alertness.
900c82e8-9a30-493c-895e-a9375263c9ab.safety_warning: May cause lightheadedness. Practice seated or lying down first.

instructions.instruction: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Take 20-30 rapid burst breaths through nose.
Each breath is like a quick sniff - sharp and quick.
After the bursts, exhale completely and hold.
Hold empty as long as comfortable.
Resume normal breathing. Repeat 2-3 rounds.

72fa1046-66e4-42cf-8c0d-9d8ca1776399.name: Buteyko Method
72fa1046-66e4-42cf-8c0d-9d8ca1776399.description: Developed by Dr. Buteyko. Focuses on nasal breathing and reducing over-breathing.
72fa1046-66e4-42cf-8c0d-9d8ca1776399.history: Developed by Dr. Buteyko for asthma and nasal breathing.
72fa1046-66e4-42cf-8c0d-9d8ca1776399.safety_warning: Do not push past mild discomfort. Not suitable during asthma attacks.

instructions.instruction: Sit comfortably and relax your body.
Close your mouth and breathe only through your nose.
Take a normal breath in and a normal breath out.
Pinch your nose and hold your breath.
When you feel the first urge to breathe, release and breathe normally.
Wait 30 seconds. Repeat, trying to extend the comfortable hold.

tips: Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable

f5b97978-6c86-46c6-af89-eded3e1e0079.name: Chandra Bhedana
f5b97978-6c86-46c6-af89-eded3e1e0079.description: Left nostril breathing to activate the lunar/cooling/calming channel.
f5b97978-6c86-46c6-af89-eded3e1e0079.history: Moon-piercing breath from Hatha Yoga - activates Ida nadi (lunar channel).
f5b97978-6c86-46c6-af89-eded3e1e0079.safety_warning: Avoid if you have low blood pressure or depression. Best done in evening.

instructions.instruction: Sit comfortably with spine straight.
Close your right nostril with thumb.
Inhale slowly through left nostril only.
Close both nostrils and hold briefly.
Exhale through right nostril.
Repeat: always inhale left, exhale right.

623aa462-aaa5-482c-a00e-f8c4542ffe71.name: Coherent Breathing
623aa462-aaa5-482c-a00e-f8c4542ffe71.description: Breathe at 5 breaths per minute to synchronize heart, brain, and nervous system.
623aa462-aaa5-482c-a00e-f8c4542ffe71.history: Breathing at 5.5 breaths/min for optimal HRV and coherence.

instructions.instruction: Sit comfortably and relax your body.
Inhale slowly for 6 seconds.
Exhale slowly for 6 seconds.
There is no pause between inhale and exhale.
Continue this smooth, even rhythm.
This rate creates optimal heart rate variability.

tips: This rate (5.5 breaths/min) optimizes heart rate variability
Most calming breathing rate for most people

a0cb55cf-81d7-4e1c-bd24-1afcca7946a5.name: Dahn Jon Breathing
a0cb55cf-81d7-4e1c-bd24-1afcca7946a5.description: Korean energy center breathing. Focus on the lower belly energy center (Dahn Jon).
a0cb55cf-81d7-4e1c-bd24-1afcca7946a5.history: From Korean Sundo tradition, dating back thousands of years. Dahn Jon (단전) is the Korean equivalent of Chinese Dantian.

instructions.instruction: Sit comfortably, spine straight but relaxed.
Place both hands on lower belly, 2 inches below navel.
Inhale deeply, expanding the lower belly into your hands.
Exhale slowly, gently drawing belly inward.
Focus attention on the warmth building in your Dahn Jon.
Continue for 10-15 minutes, cultivating energy.

tips: Imagine a glowing ball of energy

888fec01-e5ea-45c2-91dd-70414db01523.name: Dan Tian Breathing
888fec01-e5ea-45c2-91dd-70414db01523.description: Ancient Chinese breathing technique focusing on the lower abdomen energy center. Calms the mind and strengthens Qi.
888fec01-e5ea-45c2-91dd-70414db01523.history: A time-tested breathing technique for wellness.
888fec01-e5ea-45c2-91dd-70414db01523.safety_warning: Breathe gently and do not strain. Stop and return to normal breathing if you feel dizzy, lightheaded, short of breath, or anxious. Use extra caution if you have significant respiratory or cardiac conditions, and practice seated if you are prone to fainting.

instructions.instruction: Sit or stand with spine straight, shoulders relaxed.
Place hands on lower belly, 2 inches below navel (Dan Tian).
Breathe in slowly through nose, expanding the belly.
Feel the breath fill your Dan Tian energy center.
Exhale slowly, gently contracting the belly.
Visualize warm golden light in your center.

tips: Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable

27b7963f-aaff-42b4-ac0d-c04015b9d6fc.name: Diaphragmatic Breathing
27b7963f-aaff-42b4-ac0d-c04015b9d6fc.description: Strengthens the diaphragm and decreases oxygen demand. Great for stress relief and core engagement.
27b7963f-aaff-42b4-ac0d-c04015b9d6fc.history: Foundation of all breathing practices, natural deep breathing.
27b7963f-aaff-42b4-ac0d-c04015b9d6fc.safety_warning: Keep breaths comfortable—avoid forcing deep inhalations. Stop and return to normal breathing if you feel dizzy, tingling, or short of breath. Practice seated or lying down if you are prone to lightheadedness; consult a clinician if you have uncontrolled asthma/COPD or significant heart disease.

instructions.instruction: Lie on your back with knees bent, or sit comfortably.
Place one hand on your chest and one on your belly.
Breathe in slowly through your nose, feeling your belly rise.
Your chest should remain relatively still.
Exhale slowly through pursed lips, feeling your belly fall.
Continue for the duration, focusing on belly movement.

tips: Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable

028c74ef-06d4-4e7a-8202-22a0c5ccfc5e.name: Didgeridoo Circular Breath
028c74ef-06d4-4e7a-8202-22a0c5ccfc5e.description: Aboriginal breathing technique for continuous airflow. Originally for playing didgeridoo.
028c74ef-06d4-4e7a-8202-22a0c5ccfc5e.history: Essential technique for playing the didgeridoo, the world's oldest wind instrument (40,000+ years). Studies show didgeridoo playing treats sleep apnea.
028c74ef-06d4-4e7a-8202-22a0c5ccfc5e.safety_warning: May cause dizziness at first. Practice seated.

instructions.instruction: Sit comfortably with good posture.
Fill your cheeks with air like a chipmunk.
While pushing air out with cheeks, quickly inhale through nose.
Practice the coordination: cheeks push out while nose breathes in.
Start with short sessions - this takes weeks to master.
Eventually create continuous airflow without pausing.

tips: Be patient - takes weeks to learn
Practice with a straw in water first

355ce88b-d4c7-4a8b-9625-7da936c48bf9.name: Dreamtime Breath
355ce88b-d4c7-4a8b-9625-7da936c48bf9.description: Aboriginal-inspired meditation breathing for connecting with the eternal Dreamtime.
355ce88b-d4c7-4a8b-9625-7da936c48bf9.history: Inspired by Aboriginal concept of Dreamtime (Tjukurpa) - the eternal time of creation where past, present, and future coexist.
355ce88b-d4c7-4a8b-9625-7da936c48bf9.safety_warning: If practicing outdoors, choose a safe, comfortable surface and avoid extreme temperatures. Breathe gently and stop if you feel dizzy, lightheaded, or uncomfortable; practice seated if you are prone to fainting.

instructions.instruction: Sit or lie on the earth if possible (grass, sand, soil).
Close eyes and feel your body connecting with the land.
Breathe slowly, imagining roots growing from your body into earth.
With each inhale, draw up ancient wisdom from the land.
With each exhale, release your story into the earth.
Rest in timeless awareness, connected to all ancestors.

0692fb3a-9d73-42ef-b96e-91f5d3bd638f.name: Eagle Breath
0692fb3a-9d73-42ef-b96e-91f5d3bd638f.description: Expansive breathing invoking the spirit of the eagle for vision and freedom.
0692fb3a-9d73-42ef-b96e-91f5d3bd638f.history: The eagle is sacred in many Native traditions, representing connection to Creator and higher perspective.

instructions.instruction: Stand tall with arms at sides.
Inhale slowly, raising arms out to sides like wings.
At full inhale, arms are fully extended, chest open.
Hold briefly, feeling expansive like an eagle soaring.
Exhale slowly, lowering wings/arms.
Repeat 10 times, feeling freedom and expanded vision.

tips: Look upward at peak of inhale

bdf4c867-21f0-4cd9-a19d-d928b1133fd9.name: Five Element Breathing
bdf4c867-21f0-4cd9-a19d-d928b1133fd9.description: Cycle through the five elements of TCM to balance all organ systems and emotions.
bdf4c867-21f0-4cd9-a19d-d928b1133fd9.history: A time-tested breathing technique for wellness.

instructions.instruction: Wood (Liver): Breathe green, release anger. 5 breaths.
Fire (Heart): Breathe red, cultivate joy. 5 breaths.
Earth (Spleen): Breathe yellow, find stability. 5 breaths.
Metal (Lungs): Breathe white, let go of grief. 5 breaths.
Water (Kidneys): Breathe blue, release fear. 5 breaths.
Repeat the full cycle 2-3 times.

tips: Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable

4a7c6dab-c5c0-4365-bb52-fa14ebdf16ed.name: Four Directions Breath
4a7c6dab-c5c0-4365-bb52-fa14ebdf16ed.description: Native American medicine wheel breathing honoring the four sacred directions.
4a7c6dab-c5c0-4365-bb52-fa14ebdf16ed.history: Based on the Medicine Wheel, sacred to many Native American traditions. Each direction carries specific spiritual meaning.

instructions.instruction: Stand or sit facing East, the direction of new beginnings.
Inhale facing East, inviting illumination and clarity.
Turn to South. Inhale, inviting warmth and innocence.
Turn to West. Inhale, inviting introspection and transformation.
Turn to North. Inhale, inviting wisdom and endurance.
Return to East. Complete 4 full cycles of all directions.

343eac0b-0d9d-425a-a2a9-3701178b9848.name: Ha Breath
343eac0b-0d9d-425a-a2a9-3701178b9848.description: Sacred Hawaiian breath of life. 'Ha' means breath and life force in Hawaiian.
343eac0b-0d9d-425a-a2a9-3701178b9848.history: Hawaiian breath of life, sacred in Huna tradition.

instructions.instruction: Stand or sit with your feet connected to the earth.
Take a deep breath in through your nose.
Exhale forcefully through your mouth with the sound 'HA!'.
Feel the release of tension with each powerful exhale.
Repeat 7-10 times, building energy with each breath.
End with a few natural breaths, feeling revitalized.

tips: "Ha" means breath of life in Hawaiian
Used in Huna tradition for clearing energy

87bbad1e-eda2-4189-b28f-2e11ff4de2a1.name: Hara Breathing
87bbad1e-eda2-4189-b28f-2e11ff4de2a1.description: Japanese practice focusing on the body's center of gravity, 3 fingers below the navel.
87bbad1e-eda2-4189-b28f-2e11ff4de2a1.history: Breathing into the hara (belly center) in martial arts.

instructions.instruction: Sit in seiza (kneeling) or cross-legged position.
Place your attention on your hara, 3 fingers below your navel.
Breathe deeply, directing each breath to your hara.
Feel your lower belly expand on inhale, contract on exhale.
Imagine your hara as your center of power and stability.
Continue breathing into this center, feeling grounded.

tips: Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable

7b1bb204-383c-4e31-bba2-9aa0a88f528a.name: Heart Breath
7b1bb204-383c-4e31-bba2-9aa0a88f528a.description: Sufi meditation focusing on the spiritual heart. Cultivates love and divine connection.
7b1bb204-383c-4e31-bba2-9aa0a88f528a.history: Sufi practice focusing breath on the heart center.
7b1bb204-383c-4e31-bba2-9aa0a88f528a.safety_warning: If you feel lightheaded, anxious, or short of breath, return to normal breathing and stop. Practice seated if you are prone to dizziness.

instructions.instruction: Sit comfortably and place your right hand over your heart.
Close your eyes and bring attention to your heart center.
Breathe slowly, imagining breath flowing in and out of your heart.
With each inhale, breathe in love and peace.
With each exhale, release any heaviness or worry.
Feel your heart expanding with each breath cycle.

tips: Focus on feelings of love and gratitude
Can be done anytime you need centering
Sufi tradition: breath is connection to divine

ff7d31b1-6ec3-42ab-8688-e7d2070533ca.name: Holotropic Breathwork
ff7d31b1-6ec3-42ab-8688-e7d2070533ca.description: Created by Stanislav Grof. Intensive breathing for accessing non-ordinary states of consciousness.
ff7d31b1-6ec3-42ab-8688-e7d2070533ca.history: Created by Stanislav Grof for accessing altered states.
ff7d31b1-6ec3-42ab-8688-e7d2070533ca.safety_warning: Only practice with trained facilitator. Not for pregnancy, heart conditions, epilepsy, or mental illness.

instructions.instruction: Lie down in a safe, comfortable space with a sitter present.
Begin breathing faster and deeper than normal, with no pauses.
Maintain continuous circular breathing: inhale flows into exhale.
Allow any emotions, sensations, or movements to arise.
Continue for 30-60 minutes with evocative music.
Gradually slow breathing and rest. Integration is important.

tips: Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable

86f810a8-62ff-4807-b4ba-74ed32d23722.name: Holotropic Light
86f810a8-62ff-4807-b4ba-74ed32d23722.description: Simplified version of Holotropic breathwork for emotional release.
86f810a8-62ff-4807-b4ba-74ed32d23722.history: Developed by Stanislav Grof (Czech-American, working in Brazil). Uses accelerated breathing to access non-ordinary states of consciousness.
86f810a8-62ff-4807-b4ba-74ed32d23722.safety_warning: Powerful technique that can bring up intense emotions. Best with a trained facilitator. Not for pregnancy, heart conditions, or mental health conditions.

instructions.instruction: Lie down in a safe, comfortable space.
Begin breathing faster and deeper than normal - circular breath.
No pause between inhale and exhale.
Continue for 15-20 minutes without stopping.
Allow any emotions or sensations to arise and release.
Slow down gradually and rest for 10 minutes after.

659c38f4-6b52-4037-a96b-389db1a60749.name: Hygge Breath
659c38f4-6b52-4037-a96b-389db1a60749.description: Danish cozy breathing for contentment and present-moment comfort.
659c38f4-6b52-4037-a96b-389db1a60749.history: Hygge (pronounced hoo-ga) is the Danish concept of cozy contentment. This breathing practice embodies the hygge lifestyle.
659c38f4-6b52-4037-a96b-389db1a60749.safety_warning: Keep breathing gentle and unforced. Stop if you feel lightheaded or uncomfortable, and avoid candles if you may fall asleep.

instructions.instruction: Create a cozy environment - candles, blanket, warm drink nearby.
Sit or lie comfortably, allowing body to fully relax.
Breathe slowly and naturally, no effort or counting.
With each exhale, let go of any need to be anywhere else.
Feel deep contentment with this moment exactly as it is.
Continue for 10 minutes, cultivating coziness and gratitude.

1c407f50-1a77-435b-8f54-375562943657.name: Jang Saeng Breathing
1c407f50-1a77-435b-8f54-375562943657.description: Korean longevity breath for health and vitality. Ancient Sundo practice.
1c407f50-1a77-435b-8f54-375562943657.history: From Korean mountain hermit (Sundo) tradition for achieving longevity and spiritual development.
1c407f50-1a77-435b-8f54-375562943657.safety_warning: Includes a breath hold. Skip the hold or shorten it if you feel dizzy, anxious, or short of breath. Do not practice breath holds if pregnant, or if you have uncontrolled high blood pressure, significant heart/lung conditions, or a history of fainting—check with a clinician if unsure. Practice seated and stop if symptoms occur.

instructions.instruction: Sit in half-lotus or comfortable cross-legged position.
Straighten spine, tuck chin slightly, relax shoulders.
Inhale for 5 counts, filling from belly to chest.
Hold breath for 5 counts, concentrating on third eye.
Exhale for 10 counts, emptying from chest to belly.
Visualize golden light filling your body on inhale.

b7ca5e6c-ec2e-483f-a817-e9816c3be10d.name: Kapalbhati
b7ca5e6c-ec2e-483f-a817-e9816c3be10d.description: Skull Shining Breath. A powerful cleansing technique using rapid, forceful exhales.
b7ca5e6c-ec2e-483f-a817-e9816c3be10d.history: Skull-shining breath from Hatha Yoga, a purification technique.
b7ca5e6c-ec2e-483f-a817-e9816c3be10d.safety_warning: Avoid during pregnancy, menstruation, high blood pressure, or heart conditions. Stop if dizzy.

instructions.instruction: Sit with spine straight, hands on knees.
Take a deep breath in to prepare.
Exhale forcefully through your nose, pulling your navel toward spine.
Let the inhale happen passively as your belly relaxes.
Start with 20 rapid exhales, then rest with normal breathing.
Gradually increase to 60-100 exhales per round.

tips: Focus on the exhale - inhale is passive
Keep your chest and shoulders still

2bd0942d-f2db-4d36-b563-c95f1b3cef76.name: Kidney Breathing
2bd0942d-f2db-4d36-b563-c95f1b3cef76.description: TCM practice to nourish Kidney Qi and reduce fear and anxiety. Supports adrenal health.
2bd0942d-f2db-4d36-b563-c95f1b3cef76.history: A time-tested breathing technique for wellness.
2bd0942d-f2db-4d36-b563-c95f1b3cef76.safety_warning: Keep the breath comfortable and avoid straining. Stop if you feel dizzy, short of breath, or unwell; practice seated if you are prone to lightheadedness.

instructions.instruction: Sit comfortably, place hands on lower back over kidneys.
Breathe in, visualize energy flowing to your kidneys.
Hold briefly, feel warmth in lower back.
Exhale slowly, releasing fear and tension.
Repeat, building warmth and vitality.

tips: Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable

3c7f37bf-a286-4607-991b-e10bb0b4f3b6.name: Kumbhaka
3c7f37bf-a286-4607-991b-e10bb0b4f3b6.description: Extended breath retention practice to increase lung capacity and calm the mind.
3c7f37bf-a286-4607-991b-e10bb0b4f3b6.history: Ancient yogic practice mentioned in Patanjali's Yoga Sutras for mastering prana.
3c7f37bf-a286-4607-991b-e10bb0b4f3b6.safety_warning: Do not strain. Build up retention time gradually over weeks. Stop if uncomfortable.

instructions.instruction: Sit comfortably with spine straight.
Inhale deeply for 4 counts.
Hold your breath (Kumbhaka) for 8-16 counts.
Exhale slowly for 8 counts.
Optional: hold empty for 4 counts.
Repeat, gradually increasing retention time.

e8863212-5694-44b0-8864-a25feb84dc96.name: Lion's Breath
e8863212-5694-44b0-8864-a25feb84dc96.description: A playful yoga breath that releases tension in face and throat while activating the vagus nerve.
e8863212-5694-44b0-8864-a25feb84dc96.history: Simhasana from Yoga, releases tension through fierce exhale.
e8863212-5694-44b0-8864-a25feb84dc96.safety_warning: Exhale forcefully only as comfortable. Stop if you feel dizzy, cough, jaw pain, or throat irritation; practice seated if you are prone to lightheadedness.

instructions.instruction: Sit comfortably or kneel on the floor.
Take a deep breath in through your nose.
Open your mouth wide, stick out your tongue toward your chin.
Exhale forcefully with a 'HA' sound, like a lion roaring.
Widen your eyes and look upward during the exhale.
Repeat 5-7 times. Let yourself be playful!

tips: Let go of embarrassment - this is liberating
Great for releasing jaw tension and stress

628ec143-0f73-4ba8-91d0-f5a1d7ef0865.name: Nadi Shodhana
628ec143-0f73-4ba8-91d0-f5a1d7ef0865.description: Channel Purification Breath. Alternate nostril breathing for balance and mental clarity.
628ec143-0f73-4ba8-91d0-f5a1d7ef0865.history: Ancient pranayama technique from Yoga tradition (~3000 BCE).
628ec143-0f73-4ba8-91d0-f5a1d7ef0865.safety_warning: Avoid if you have a cold or nasal congestion.

instructions.instruction: Sit comfortably with spine straight.
Use right thumb to close right nostril.
Inhale slowly through left nostril for 4 counts.
Close left nostril with ring finger, hold for 4 counts.
Release right nostril, exhale for 4 counts.
Inhale right, hold, exhale left. This is one round.
Continue for 5-10 rounds.

tips: Balances left and right brain hemispheres
Great for focus and calming anxiety

7922c669-772a-4242-b5a5-0701c6810867.name: Nine-Round Breathing
7922c669-772a-4242-b5a5-0701c6810867.description: Tibetan Buddhist purification practice to clear energy channels and calm the mind.
7922c669-772a-4242-b5a5-0701c6810867.history: Buddhist practice to purify negative energies through 9 breaths.
7922c669-772a-4242-b5a5-0701c6810867.safety_warning: Breathe gently and do not force the breath. Stop if you feel dizzy, congested, or short of breath; avoid if you have significant nasal blockage or a nosebleed.

instructions.instruction: Sit comfortably with spine straight and hands on thighs.
First 3 breaths: Block right nostril, inhale left, exhale right.
Next 3 breaths: Block left nostril, inhale right, exhale left.
Last 3 breaths: Breathe through both nostrils equally.
With each exhale, visualize releasing negativity and obstacles.
Repeat the full cycle of 9 breaths 2-3 times.

tips: Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable

e6dea69c-6d9b-4fc9-898c-c106b4af850f.name: Physiological Sigh
e6dea69c-6d9b-4fc9-898c-c106b4af850f.description: The fastest way to calm down - discovered by Stanford researchers.
e6dea69c-6d9b-4fc9-898c-c106b4af850f.history: Discovered by Stanford researchers as the fastest way to calm down.
e6dea69c-6d9b-4fc9-898c-c106b4af850f.safety_warning: Do not force large breaths. Stop if you feel lightheaded, tingling, or uncomfortable; practice seated if you are prone to dizziness.

instructions.instruction: Take a deep breath in.
At the top, sneak in a second smaller breath.
Slowly exhale all the air out.
Repeat 3-5 times.

tips: The double inhale is key - it opens collapsed air sacs
Make the exhale at least twice as long as inhale
This is the fastest way to calm your nervous system

e9d652ea-e0e1-4dd5-b513-1eeb4958bd2f.name: Physiological Sigh
e9d652ea-e0e1-4dd5-b513-1eeb4958bd2f.description: The fastest way to calm down in real-time. Discovered by Stanford neuroscientist Andrew Huberman.
e9d652ea-e0e1-4dd5-b513-1eeb4958bd2f.history: Discovered by Stanford researchers as the fastest way to calm down.
e9d652ea-e0e1-4dd5-b513-1eeb4958bd2f.safety_warning: Do not force large breaths. Stop if you feel lightheaded, tingling, or uncomfortable; practice seated if you are prone to dizziness.

instructions.instruction: This can be done anywhere, anytime you feel stressed.
Inhale deeply through your nose.
At the top, take a second quick inhale to fully fill your lungs.
Exhale slowly and completely through your mouth.
The double inhale reopens collapsed air sacs in your lungs.
Repeat 1-3 times for immediate calm.

tips: The double inhale is key - it opens collapsed air sacs
Make the exhale at least twice as long as inhale
This is the fastest way to calm your nervous system

791d6e1d-d276-4ea5-822c-9d314660be61.name: Pranayama Bali
791d6e1d-d276-4ea5-822c-9d314660be61.description: Balinese temple breathing for spiritual cleansing and connection with nature spirits.
791d6e1d-d276-4ea5-822c-9d314660be61.history: Balinese Hindu breathing practice (Pranayama) adapted with local animist traditions. Part of daily temple offerings ritual.
791d6e1d-d276-4ea5-822c-9d314660be61.safety_warning: If you feel lightheaded, anxious, or short of breath, return to normal breathing and stop. Avoid breath holds if you are pregnant or have uncontrolled high blood pressure, heart rhythm problems, or a history of fainting unless cleared by a clinician.

instructions.instruction: Sit facing the rising sun or natural beauty.
Close eyes and feel connection with nature around you.
Inhale slowly, imagining drawing in energy from nature.
Hold briefly, feeling gratitude in your heart.
Exhale releasing any negative energy back to earth for transformation.
Continue with deep reverence for the natural world.

9514882e-da33-4c97-b547-fe8f18a86cc8.name: Qigong Breathing
9514882e-da33-4c97-b547-fe8f18a86cc8.description: Ancient Chinese practice combining breath, movement, and energy visualization for healing.
9514882e-da33-4c97-b547-fe8f18a86cc8.history: Core Qigong practice focusing on the energy center below navel.
9514882e-da33-4c97-b547-fe8f18a86cc8.safety_warning: Breathe comfortably—do not strain or force big breaths. Stop and return to normal breathing if you feel dizzy, tingling, chest discomfort, or anxiety; practice seated if you are prone to lightheadedness.

instructions.instruction: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent.
Place your hands on your lower belly (dantian).
Breathe deeply into your belly, feeling it expand under your hands.
As you inhale, visualize gathering energy from the earth.
As you exhale, imagine releasing tension and stagnant energy.
Continue with slow, deep breaths, feeling rooted and calm.

tips: Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable

409ab72c-8c33-4044-a0fa-6754e3a56dbc.name: Quick Calm
409ab72c-8c33-4044-a0fa-6754e3a56dbc.description: A 1-minute breathing reset to instantly reduce stress. Perfect for busy moments.
409ab72c-8c33-4044-a0fa-6754e3a56dbc.history: A time-tested breathing technique for wellness.
409ab72c-8c33-4044-a0fa-6754e3a56dbc.safety_warning: Keep the breath gentle and comfortable. If you feel lightheaded or air-hungry, shorten the counts or return to normal breathing and stop.

instructions.instruction: Close your eyes and take a deep breath.
Breathe in for 4 counts, out for 6 counts.
Focus only on your breath.
Continue until the session ends.

tips: Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable

882fb6dd-c808-4de7-91ea-c26cd613a4af.name: Resonant Breathing
882fb6dd-c808-4de7-91ea-c26cd613a4af.description: Syncs your breath with your heart rate for maximum calm. Achieves heart coherence at ~5 breaths per minute.
882fb6dd-c808-4de7-91ea-c26cd613a4af.history: Breathing at 5.5 breaths/min for optimal HRV and coherence.
882fb6dd-c808-4de7-91ea-c26cd613a4af.safety_warning: Do not force the timing—use a shorter, comfortable count if needed. Stop if you feel dizzy, breathless, or uncomfortable, and return to normal breathing; use caution if you have COPD/asthma or are prone to fainting.

instructions.instruction: Find a comfortable seated position.
Inhale slowly for 6 seconds.
Exhale slowly for 6 seconds.
Maintain this rhythm without pausing between breaths.
Focus on the smooth, continuous flow of breath.

tips: This rate (5.5 breaths/min) optimizes heart rate variability
Most calming breathing rate for most people

57de4961-2181-4b30-b71e-d77b39ad6903.name: Reverse Breathing
57de4961-2181-4b30-b71e-d77b39ad6903.description: Taoist technique where the abdomen contracts on inhale. Builds internal power and focus.
57de4961-2181-4b30-b71e-d77b39ad6903.history: Taoist technique where abdomen contracts on inhale.
57de4961-2181-4b30-b71e-d77b39ad6903.safety_warning: Advanced practice. Master natural breathing first. Stop if uncomfortable.

instructions.instruction: Sit or stand in a relaxed posture.
Place one hand on your belly to feel the movement.
As you inhale, gently draw your belly IN toward spine.
As you exhale, let your belly expand OUT.
This is the reverse of natural breathing.
Practice slowly, 10-15 breaths. It takes time to master.

tips: Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable

1f49d6a2-53bd-4a8a-9f65-84121d4ae485.name: Ruesri Dat Ton Breath
1f49d6a2-53bd-4a8a-9f65-84121d4ae485.description: Thai yoga breathing for self-healing. Ancient hermit sage techniques.
1f49d6a2-53bd-4a8a-9f65-84121d4ae485.history: Ruesri Dat Ton is Thai yoga, practiced by hermit sages (ruesri) for thousands of years. Combines breath with self-massage and movement.
1f49d6a2-53bd-4a8a-9f65-84121d4ae485.safety_warning: Move within a pain-free range and avoid forcing the neck or low back. Skip the breath hold and keep breathing if you feel dizzy; avoid kneeling/arching positions if they worsen knee, back, or neck symptoms.

instructions.instruction: Sit in diamond pose (kneeling with buttocks on heels).
Place hands on thighs, spine straight.
Inhale slowly, arching back and looking upward.
Hold briefly at the top.
Exhale, rounding spine and tucking chin to chest.
Coordinate breath with spinal movement for 10 minutes.

tips: Movement and breath should be smooth

a6dfe711-e70a-47e9-8e58-45c20835807e.name: Sitali Pranayama
a6dfe711-e70a-47e9-8e58-45c20835807e.description: Cooling Breath. Roll your tongue and breathe to cool the body and calm emotions.
a6dfe711-e70a-47e9-8e58-45c20835807e.history: Cooling breath from ancient Hatha Yoga tradition.
a6dfe711-e70a-47e9-8e58-45c20835807e.safety_warning: Avoid in cold weather or if you have asthma or respiratory infections.

instructions.instruction: Sit comfortably with eyes closed.
Roll your tongue into a tube shape (or purse lips if unable).
Inhale slowly through your rolled tongue, feeling cool air.
Close your mouth and exhale through your nose.
Notice the cooling sensation on your tongue and throat.
Repeat for 10-15 breaths.

tips: Cools the body and calms the mind
Good for hot weather or anger
Avoid in cold weather or with respiratory issues

aac8b050-7afa-4dc2-80ce-302fb2258884.name: Steppe Wind Breath
aac8b050-7afa-4dc2-80ce-302fb2258884.description: Mongolian breathing inspired by the vast open steppes. Expansive and grounding.
aac8b050-7afa-4dc2-80ce-302fb2258884.history: Inspired by Mongolian nomadic culture where the vast steppe and sky create a unique sense of spaciousness and freedom.
aac8b050-7afa-4dc2-80ce-302fb2258884.safety_warning: Keep breaths slow and comfortable—avoid over-breathing. If you feel lightheaded, unsteady, or anxious, stop and return to normal breathing; practice seated if needed.

instructions.instruction: Stand or sit facing open space (or visualize vast plains).
Inhale slowly, imagining the endless horizon expanding.
Let your awareness expand with the breath to the horizon.
Exhale, feeling grounded like a mountain on the steppe.
Feel both vast and grounded simultaneously.
Continue, connecting with the spirit of endless space.

tips: Feel small and vast at once

aa482f3b-c1ad-4776-beb6-de5f9802e720.name: Stress Buster
aa482f3b-c1ad-4776-beb6-de5f9802e720.description: Fast-acting breathing technique to lower cortisol in 2 minutes.
aa482f3b-c1ad-4776-beb6-de5f9802e720.history: A time-tested breathing technique for wellness.
aa482f3b-c1ad-4776-beb6-de5f9802e720.safety_warning: Quick breaths can cause dizziness or tingling in some people. Keep the inhales small, prioritize a comfortable long exhale, and stop if you feel lightheaded, panicky, or unwell; avoid if it triggers asthma symptoms.

instructions.instruction: Sit or stand comfortably.
Take 3 quick breaths in through nose.
One long exhale through mouth.
Repeat for the duration.

tips: Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable

a44a055c-6bfe-432f-b069-c0c115ac2399.name: Surya Bhedana
a44a055c-6bfe-432f-b069-c0c115ac2399.description: Right nostril breathing to activate the solar/heating/energizing channel.
a44a055c-6bfe-432f-b069-c0c115ac2399.history: Sun-piercing breath from Hatha Yoga - activates Pingala nadi (solar channel).
a44a055c-6bfe-432f-b069-c0c115ac2399.safety_warning: Avoid if you have high blood pressure or heart conditions. Best done in morning.

instructions.instruction: Sit comfortably with spine straight.
Close your left nostril with ring finger.
Inhale slowly through right nostril only.
Close both nostrils and hold briefly.
Exhale through left nostril.
Repeat: always inhale right, exhale left.

4e81ff72-6c03-466a-8a53-69a87f5b8eb9.name: Systema Breathing
4e81ff72-6c03-466a-8a53-69a87f5b8eb9.description: Russian martial arts breathing for stress resilience and recovery. Used by Spetsnaz special forces.
4e81ff72-6c03-466a-8a53-69a87f5b8eb9.history: Developed from ancient Russian Orthodox breathing practices, refined by Mikhail Ryabko for Systema martial arts. Used by Russian special forces for extreme stress management.
4e81ff72-6c03-466a-8a53-69a87f5b8eb9.safety_warning: Avoid forcing fast breathing; it can cause dizziness or anxiety. If you feel lightheaded, numb/tingly, or short of breath, slow down or stop and return to normal breathing; seek medical advice if symptoms persist.

instructions.instruction: Stand or sit naturally, completely relaxed.
Inhale through nose, exhale through mouth - continuous flow.
Match breath to movement or stress level.
Under stress: short quick breaths. Calm: long slow breaths.
Never hold your breath, keep it flowing.
Practice recovery breathing: deep inhale, very long exhale.

tips: Exhale longer than inhale for calm
Can be practiced during any activity

5f7d38df-f537-4f07-ad76-a63ed291d8d7.name: Temazcal Breath
5f7d38df-f537-4f07-ad76-a63ed291d8d7.description: Mexican sweat lodge breathing for purification and rebirth.
5f7d38df-f537-4f07-ad76-a63ed291d8d7.history: Temazcal is an ancient Mesoamerican sweat lodge ceremony used by Aztec, Maya, and other indigenous peoples for healing and spiritual purification.
5f7d38df-f537-4f07-ad76-a63ed291d8d7.safety_warning: Stay hydrated. Exit heat if feeling unwell. Not for pregnancy or heart conditions.

instructions.instruction: Sit in a warm, enclosed space (hot bath, sauna, or warm room).
Close eyes and connect with the heat around you.
Breathe slowly through nose, accepting the heat.
With each exhale, release toxins and old patterns.
Visualize emerging reborn and purified.
If doing in actual heat, limit to 15-20 minutes.

tips: Can practice the breath without actual heat

d1ec4bb1-6ddd-40d8-b30f-6e3ec8713383.name: Tenaga Dalam
d1ec4bb1-6ddd-40d8-b30f-6e3ec8713383.description: Indonesian inner power breathing. Martial arts technique for cultivating internal energy.
d1ec4bb1-6ddd-40d8-b30f-6e3ec8713383.history: From Indonesian Pencak Silat martial arts. Tenaga Dalam means "inner power" - cultivating chi/prana through breath and tension.
d1ec4bb1-6ddd-40d8-b30f-6e3ec8713383.safety_warning: Do not practice with high blood pressure or heart conditions.

instructions.instruction: Stand in horse stance or sit in meditation posture.
Breathe deeply into lower belly with full attention.
On inhale, tense muscles progressively from feet upward.
Hold breath and full tension for 5-10 seconds.
Exhale explosively, releasing all tension at once.
Feel the energy circulating. Repeat 7 times.

db6df80c-7266-4fa0-9289-62fc5c3555d3.name: Tummo Breathing
db6df80c-7266-4fa0-9289-62fc5c3555d3.description: Inner Fire meditation. Advanced Tibetan technique for generating inner heat and energy.
db6df80c-7266-4fa0-9289-62fc5c3555d3.history: Inner fire meditation from Tibetan Buddhism for generating heat.
db6df80c-7266-4fa0-9289-62fc5c3555d3.safety_warning: This is an advanced practice. Learn from a qualified teacher. Stop if uncomfortable.

instructions.instruction: Sit in a comfortable meditative posture.
Visualize a small flame at your navel center.
Inhale deeply, drawing energy down to the flame.
Hold the breath and visualize the flame growing brighter.
Exhale slowly, feeling warmth spreading through your body.
Continue, gradually building the sensation of inner heat.

tips: Learn from qualified teacher for full practice

09b991d2-6238-4c0d-a156-99a77a3cf5bb.name: Turtle Breathing
09b991d2-6238-4c0d-a156-99a77a3cf5bb.description: Ancient Taoist longevity practice. Extremely slow breaths inspired by the turtle's lifespan.
09b991d2-6238-4c0d-a156-99a77a3cf5bb.history: Ancient Taoist practice for longevity, inspired by turtle's slow breath.
09b991d2-6238-4c0d-a156-99a77a3cf5bb.safety_warning: Very advanced practice. Only attempt after years of breath training.

instructions.instruction: Sit in deep meditation posture, completely relaxed.
Begin with normal breaths, gradually slowing them down.
Aim for breaths so slow they are almost imperceptible.
Inhale for 15-30 seconds or more.
Exhale equally slowly, with no pause between.
Let the breath become thread-like, almost stopping.

tips: Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable

6b503756-4be6-49dc-a60b-49839d6bb215.name: Ubuntu Breath
6b503756-4be6-49dc-a60b-49839d6bb215.description: African communal breathing practice. "I am because we are" - breathing in connection with others.
6b503756-4be6-49dc-a60b-49839d6bb215.history: Based on Ubuntu philosophy from Southern Africa. Ubuntu means "humanity toward others" - the belief in universal bond of sharing.
6b503756-4be6-49dc-a60b-49839d6bb215.safety_warning: Keep the breath natural and comfortable. Stop if you feel dizzy, lightheaded, anxious, or short of breath. If you have a respiratory or cardiac condition, practice gently and consider checking with a clinician.

instructions.instruction: Sit comfortably, ideally in a circle with others (or visualize community).
Place hand on heart and breathe naturally.
Inhale, imagining receiving love and support from your community.
Exhale, sending love and support back to your community.
Feel the interconnection with all beings.
Continue, expanding your circle to include all humanity.

tips: Focus on giving and receiving equally

b9d7ed6e-36d6-4735-9590-08da8259355f.name: Ujjayi Breathing
b9d7ed6e-36d6-4735-9590-08da8259355f.description: The victorious breath from yoga tradition. Creates a soft oceanic sound by gently constricting the throat.
b9d7ed6e-36d6-4735-9590-08da8259355f.history: Ocean breath from Yoga, used in Ashtanga practice.
b9d7ed6e-36d6-4735-9590-08da8259355f.safety_warning: Start gently. If you feel strain in your throat, relax the constriction.

instructions.instruction: Sit comfortably with spine straight and shoulders relaxed.
Slightly constrict the back of your throat, as if fogging a mirror.
Breathe in slowly through your nose, creating a soft hissing sound.
Exhale through your nose with the same gentle constriction.
The breath should sound like ocean waves or a gentle snore.
Keep the breath slow, smooth, and rhythmic throughout.

tips: Imagine fogging a mirror with your breath
Keep the sound soft, not forced
Used throughout yoga practice for focus

f0ca4134-2b78-443c-962d-b465d17005e6.name: Vase Breathing
f0ca4134-2b78-443c-962d-b465d17005e6.description: Kumbhaka practice. Holding breath in the belly like a vase to retain prana and deepen meditation.
f0ca4134-2b78-443c-962d-b465d17005e6.history: Holding breath in the belly like a vase, used in Tibetan Yoga.
f0ca4134-2b78-443c-962d-b465d17005e6.safety_warning: Advanced practice. Learn from qualified teacher. Do not strain.

instructions.instruction: Sit in meditation posture with straight spine.
Inhale deeply, drawing breath down to your belly.
Swallow gently and press down, sealing the breath.
Hold the breath in your lower belly like water in a vase.
When you need to exhale, release slowly through the nose.
Rest and repeat. Start with short holds, increase gradually.

tips: Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable

92c3876c-78cf-446b-9381-f75d8af2395f.name: Viloma Pranayama
92c3876c-78cf-446b-9381-f75d8af2395f.description: Interrupted breathing - inhale or exhale in stages with pauses.
92c3876c-78cf-446b-9381-f75d8af2395f.history: Classical pranayama meaning 'against the grain' - interrupting natural breath flow.
92c3876c-78cf-446b-9381-f75d8af2395f.safety_warning: Avoid if you have anxiety or panic disorder. Keep pauses gentle.

instructions.instruction: Lie down or sit comfortably.
Inhale for 2 seconds, pause for 2 seconds.
Inhale more for 2 seconds, pause again.
Continue until lungs are full (3-4 stages).
Exhale smoothly and completely.
Repeat 5-10 cycles. Can also do interrupted exhale.

tips: Can do interrupted inhale OR exhale

9e2e5d34-5f47-44ee-81e9-f6d31d979017.name: Wim Hof Breathing
9e2e5d34-5f47-44ee-81e9-f6d31d979017.description: Powerful breathing method for energy, focus, and stress resilience. Created by 'The Iceman'.
9e2e5d34-5f47-44ee-81e9-f6d31d979017.history: Created by Wim Hof combining breathing, cold, and commitment.
9e2e5d34-5f47-44ee-81e9-f6d31d979017.safety_warning: Never practice in water or while driving. Lie down in a safe place. Tingling is normal; stop if uncomfortable.

instructions.instruction: Lie down or sit comfortably in a safe place.
Take 30-40 deep breaths: inhale fully, exhale without forcing.
On the last exhale, hold your breath with empty lungs.
Hold as long as comfortable (1-3 minutes).
When you need to breathe, inhale fully and hold for 15 seconds.
Exhale and repeat the cycle 3-4 times.

tips: Never practice in water or while driving!
The retention gets easier with practice

f832d044-9a15-461c-90f8-946fe6463ee6.name: Wim Hof Method
f832d044-9a15-461c-90f8-946fe6463ee6.description: The Ice Man technique. Combines deep breathing, breath holds, and cold exposure.
f832d044-9a15-461c-90f8-946fe6463ee6.history: Created by Wim Hof combining breathing, cold, and commitment.
f832d044-9a15-461c-90f8-946fe6463ee6.safety_warning: Never practice in water or while driving. May cause lightheadedness. Lie down for safety.

instructions.instruction: Lie down or sit comfortably in a safe place.
Take 30-40 deep, powerful breaths: full inhale, relaxed exhale.
On the last exhale, hold your breath with lungs empty.
Hold as long as comfortable (1-3 minutes is normal).
When you need to breathe, take one deep breath and hold 15 seconds.
Exhale and repeat 3-4 rounds. Optional: follow with cold exposure.

tips: Never practice in water or while driving!
The retention gets easier with practice

c2007bf4-802e-41ed-ac84-2f3d5d032e35.name: Yoruba Ase Breathing
c2007bf4-802e-41ed-ac84-2f3d5d032e35.description: Nigerian spiritual breathing to activate Ase - the life force and power to make things happen.
c2007bf4-802e-41ed-ac84-2f3d5d032e35.history: From Yoruba spiritual tradition of Nigeria. Ase (also Ashe) is the divine life force that flows through all things.
c2007bf4-802e-41ed-ac84-2f3d5d032e35.safety_warning: Use a soft whisper and avoid straining or forcing deep breaths. Stop if you feel dizzy, tingling, or uncomfortable. If you have asthma/COPD, vocal strain issues, or a heart condition, practice gently and consider medical guidance.

instructions.instruction: Sit or stand with spine straight, feet grounded.
Place hands on lower belly where Ase resides.
Inhale slowly through nose, filling belly with life force.
Whisper 'Ase' (ah-shay) on the exhale.
Feel the word vibrating through your body.
Continue, setting intentions for what you wish to manifest.

181811cb-ba5b-43f0-b0fe-ba710a743e37.name: Zazen Breath Counting
181811cb-ba5b-43f0-b0fe-ba710a743e37.description: Traditional Zen meditation technique. Count breaths to anchor the wandering mind.
181811cb-ba5b-43f0-b0fe-ba710a743e37.history: Zen meditation breathing, foundation of Zazen practice.
181811cb-ba5b-43f0-b0fe-ba710a743e37.safety_warning: Breathe normally—do not force slow or deep breathing. If you feel dizzy, panicky, or uncomfortable, return to natural breathing or stop. If sitting causes pain or numbness, change posture or use support.

instructions.instruction: Sit in a comfortable, stable position with spine straight.
Lower your gaze to a point about 3 feet ahead, eyes half-closed.
Breathe naturally through your nose.
Count each exhale: 1, 2, 3... up to 10.
When you reach 10, start again from 1.
If you lose count, gently return to 1 without judgment.

tips: Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable

eae95e86-bd7d-4a0f-9748-fd2d1da78414.name: Zikr Breathing
eae95e86-bd7d-4a0f-9748-fd2d1da78414.description: Sufi remembrance breathing with divine names. Heart-centered devotional practice.
eae95e86-bd7d-4a0f-9748-fd2d1da78414.history: Zikr (dhikr) means remembrance of the Divine. Central practice in Sufism for polishing the heart and drawing near to God.
eae95e86-bd7d-4a0f-9748-fd2d1da78414.safety_warning: Keep breathing easy and unforced. If repetition brings distress, dizziness, or anxiety, pause and return to normal breathing. If you have a history of panic attacks, start with short sessions and a neutral word.

instructions.instruction: Sit comfortably with hand on heart.
Close eyes and breathe naturally for a minute.
On inhale, silently say a sacred word (Allah, Love, Peace).
On exhale, let the word resonate in your heart.
Continue rhythmically, word becoming automatic.
Let the remembrance fill your entire being.

tips: Use any sacred word meaningful to you
The word can become a breath itself

821665a0-61ea-4aa1-8a56-ef6fac68ed09.name: Zulu Warrior Breath
821665a0-61ea-4aa1-8a56-ef6fac68ed09.description: Powerful breathing technique for courage and strength. From Zulu warrior traditions.
821665a0-61ea-4aa1-8a56-ef6fac68ed09.history: Inspired by Zulu warrior preparation rituals. Warriors would breathe and chant together before battle.
821665a0-61ea-4aa1-8a56-ef6fac68ed09.safety_warning: This is an energizing, forceful practice—go gently and avoid hyperventilating. Stop immediately if you feel dizzy, tingling, chest pain, or short of breath. Avoid if you are pregnant, have uncontrolled high blood pressure, heart rhythm problems, glaucoma, or a history of fainting unless cleared by a clinician.

instructions.instruction: Stand tall with feet wide, hands on hips like a warrior.
Inhale powerfully through nose, expanding chest and belly.
Hold briefly, feeling your power and courage.
Exhale with a strong 'HA!' sound from deep in belly.
Stamp foot on exhale for grounding.
Repeat 10-20 times, building energy and courage.

cc01b3f3-c430-4c39-9111-489e81380749.name: Cold Water Facial Immersion
cc01b3f3-c430-4c39-9111-489e81380749.description: Triggers the diving reflex to activate the parasympathetic nervous system rapidly.
cc01b3f3-c430-4c39-9111-489e81380749.history: Ancient practice found in many cultures; popularized by Wim Hof.
cc01b3f3-c430-4c39-9111-489e81380749.safety_warning: Consult your doctor before trying this exercise if you have a heart condition or low blood pressure. Do not force yourself to hold your breath.

instructions.instruction: Fill a bowl with cold water. Add ice cubes for a more potent effect.
Take a deep breath and hold it.
Lean forward and gently submerge your face in the water.
Focus on the area around your eyes and cheeks.
Keep your face submerged for 15-30 seconds.
Come up for air and repeat 2-3 times as comfortable.
Gently pat your face dry and notice the shift in your body.

tips: Start with just 15 seconds and build up

c8f61252-9b1a-4b8b-b01d-760fe2e2730f.name: Diving Reflex
c8f61252-9b1a-4b8b-b01d-760fe2e2730f.description: Cold water on face triggers the mammalian diving reflex, instantly calming you.
c8f61252-9b1a-4b8b-b01d-760fe2e2730f.history: The diving reflex is hardwired in all mammals - it slows heart rate instantly.
c8f61252-9b1a-4b8b-b01d-760fe2e2730f.safety_warning: Avoid if you have heart conditions. Don't hold breath too long.

instructions.instruction: Fill a bowl with cold water (or use cold, wet towel).
Take a deep breath and hold it.
Submerge your face in the cold water (or apply towel).
Hold for 15-30 seconds.
Come up, breathe normally.
Repeat 2-3 times if needed.

tips: Water should be cold but not ice

69f9dcb4-d293-4230-8789-7dfa0c4044a0.name: Gargling
69f9dcb4-d293-4230-8789-7dfa0c4044a0.description: Stimulates the vagus nerve through the muscles in the back of the throat.
69f9dcb4-d293-4230-8789-7dfa0c4044a0.history: A time-tested breathing technique for wellness.
69f9dcb4-d293-4230-8789-7dfa0c4044a0.safety_warning: Use only small sips to reduce choking risk. Avoid if you have trouble swallowing, are lying down, or are at risk of aspiration. Stop if you cough, choke, feel lightheaded, or have throat pain.

instructions.instruction: Take a sip of water.
Tilt your head back slightly.
Gargle vigorously for 30-60 seconds.
Spit out the water.
Repeat 2-3 times.
You may feel a slight contraction in your throat muscles.

tips: Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable

1e08356c-7779-421d-a4ed-94bbddd6ab46.name: Mindful Drinking
1e08356c-7779-421d-a4ed-94bbddd6ab46.description: Combines slow drinking with breath awareness for gentle vagal activation.
1e08356c-7779-421d-a4ed-94bbddd6ab46.history: A time-tested breathing technique for wellness.
1e08356c-7779-421d-a4ed-94bbddd6ab46.safety_warning: Sip slowly and avoid if you have difficulty swallowing or are at risk of choking/aspiration. Stop if you cough, choke, or feel dizzy or nauseated.

instructions.instruction: Prepare a glass of room temperature water.
Hold the glass and take a moment to feel its weight and temperature.
Take a slow breath in.
Take a small sip and hold the water in your mouth for a moment.
Swallow slowly and mindfully.
Exhale slowly after swallowing.
Repeat until the glass is empty, maintaining awareness.

tips: Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable

3f9814dd-1f21-4b04-a151-e76e7a29cbfe.name: Body Scan
3f9814dd-1f21-4b04-a151-e76e7a29cbfe.description: Progressive relaxation technique to release tension and activate the rest response.
3f9814dd-1f21-4b04-a151-e76e7a29cbfe.history: A time-tested breathing technique for wellness.
3f9814dd-1f21-4b04-a151-e76e7a29cbfe.safety_warning: Stop if you feel dizzy, panicky, or uncomfortable. If lying down worsens reflux, breathing issues, or pain, switch to a supported seated position. Seek medical advice if symptoms are persistent or severe.

instructions.instruction: Lie down comfortably on your back.
Close your eyes and take 3 deep breaths.
Bring attention to your feet. Notice any sensations, then relax them.
Slowly move attention up: calves, thighs, hips, belly, chest.
Continue to shoulders, arms, hands, neck, face, and head.
Rest in full-body awareness for a few minutes.

tips: Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable

227ee00d-8201-4216-9c38-09de1cd8c5d6.name: Capoeira Ginga Breath
227ee00d-8201-4216-9c38-09de1cd8c5d6.description: Brazilian martial arts breathing synchronized with the fundamental ginga movement.
227ee00d-8201-4216-9c38-09de1cd8c5d6.history: Ginga is the fundamental movement of Capoeira, the Afro-Brazilian martial art disguised as dance. Breathing powers the continuous movement.
227ee00d-8201-4216-9c38-09de1cd8c5d6.safety_warning: Move within a pain-free range and use a stable, non-slip surface. Stop if you feel dizzy, short of breath, or have joint pain. If you have balance problems or a recent injury, consider doing a smaller range of motion or holding a chair for support.

instructions.instruction: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Step right foot back diagonally, bending both knees.
Inhale as you step back.
Return to center and step left foot back diagonally.
Exhale as you step back with left foot.
Continue the flowing ginga rhythm for 10 minutes.

278d1121-8e6a-40f5-804b-c906eb19089e.name: Eye Yoga
278d1121-8e6a-40f5-804b-c906eb19089e.description: Gentle eye movements that stimulate the vagus nerve and reduce eye strain.
278d1121-8e6a-40f5-804b-c906eb19089e.history: A gentle eye-movement practice for visual comfort and mindful focus.
278d1121-8e6a-40f5-804b-c906eb19089e.safety_warning: Keep movements gentle and pain-free. Stop if you develop dizziness, nausea, headache, or eye pain. If you have a recent eye surgery, retinal problems, or severe vertigo, check with a clinician before doing eye-movement exercises.

instructions.instruction: Sit comfortably and relax your shoulders.
Without moving your head, look up as far as comfortable, then down. Repeat 5 times.
Look left, then right. Repeat 5 times.
Look diagonally: upper left to lower right, then upper right to lower left. 5 times each.
Slowly circle your eyes clockwise 5 times, then counter-clockwise.
Close your eyes and rest for 30 seconds.

tips: Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable

999ecb46-c3c1-46a2-8d8c-bbb922ca8097.name: Five Tibetan Rites
999ecb46-c3c1-46a2-8d8c-bbb922ca8097.description: Ancient sequence of 5 movements synchronized with breath for vitality.
999ecb46-c3c1-46a2-8d8c-bbb922ca8097.history: Allegedly from Tibetan monks, popularized in 1939 book "The Eye of Revelation".
999ecb46-c3c1-46a2-8d8c-bbb922ca8097.safety_warning: Start with few repetitions. Not for pregnancy or serious back issues.

instructions.instruction: Rite 1: Spin clockwise with arms out, 21 times.
Rite 2: Lie flat, raise legs and head together, 21 times.
Rite 3: Kneel, arch back, then flex forward, 21 times.
Rite 4: Sit, raise body into table pose, 21 times.
Rite 5: Downward dog to upward dog flow, 21 times.
Start with 3-7 reps each, build to 21 over weeks.

f90760e8-b8e7-43f5-bf9b-3813aad36262.name: Legs Up The Wall
f90760e8-b8e7-43f5-bf9b-3813aad36262.description: A restorative yoga pose that activates the parasympathetic nervous system.
f90760e8-b8e7-43f5-bf9b-3813aad36262.history: A time-tested breathing technique for wellness.
f90760e8-b8e7-43f5-bf9b-3813aad36262.safety_warning: Avoid if you have glaucoma, high blood pressure, or are menstruating heavily.

instructions.instruction: Find a clear wall space and sit sideways next to it.
Swing your legs up onto the wall as you lower your back to the floor.
Scoot your hips as close to the wall as comfortable.
Rest your arms by your sides, palms facing up.
Close your eyes and breathe naturally.
Stay in this position for the duration, allowing gravity to do the work.
To exit, bend your knees and roll to one side before sitting up.

tips: Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable

bf25afa0-572f-4933-9e41-516573a05a1b.name: Lifting the Sky
bf25afa0-572f-4933-9e41-516573a05a1b.description: Simple Qigong exercise to open the chest, improve posture, and circulate Qi throughout the body.
bf25afa0-572f-4933-9e41-516573a05a1b.history: A time-tested breathing technique for wellness.
bf25afa0-572f-4933-9e41-516573a05a1b.safety_warning: Avoid forcing the stretch or locking your elbows. Stop if you feel shoulder/neck pain, dizziness, or tingling. If you have uncontrolled high blood pressure, glaucoma, or shoulder injury, keep arms lower and move gently.

instructions.instruction: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Interlace fingers, palms facing down in front of you.
Inhale, raise arms overhead, palms facing up.
Gently push palms toward sky, stretch upward.
Exhale, lower arms slowly to sides.
Repeat 8-10 times with slow breaths.

tips: Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable

112d4de0-357d-4876-9c28-4c37ce25df21.name: Neck Release
112d4de0-357d-4876-9c28-4c37ce25df21.description: Quick tension release for neck and shoulders - perfect for desk workers.
112d4de0-357d-4876-9c28-4c37ce25df21.history: A time-tested breathing technique for wellness.
112d4de0-357d-4876-9c28-4c37ce25df21.safety_warning: Stop if you feel pain or dizziness.

instructions.instruction: Drop your chin to chest, hold 10 seconds.
Slowly roll head to right shoulder.
Hold 10 seconds, feeling the stretch.
Roll to left shoulder, hold 10 seconds.
Return to center. Repeat if time allows.

tips: Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable

d81c97b5-3754-43a0-bdb7-7c819076b8b0.name: Neck Stretches
d81c97b5-3754-43a0-bdb7-7c819076b8b0.description: Gentle stretches to release tension and stimulate the vagus nerve in the neck area.
d81c97b5-3754-43a0-bdb7-7c819076b8b0.history: A time-tested breathing technique for wellness.
d81c97b5-3754-43a0-bdb7-7c819076b8b0.safety_warning: Move slowly and never force your neck into uncomfortable positions.

instructions.instruction: Sit or stand with your spine straight.
Slowly tilt your head to the right, bringing your ear toward your shoulder.
Hold for 30 seconds, breathing deeply.
Return to center and repeat on the left side.
Gently rotate your head in a circle, 5 times each direction.
Finish by tucking your chin to your chest and holding for 30 seconds.

tips: Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable

def29a93-7f64-459d-af03-4f57e460d30a.name: Shaking Qigong
def29a93-7f64-459d-af03-4f57e460d30a.description: Vibration practice to release tension, move stagnant energy, and activate the nervous system reset.
def29a93-7f64-459d-af03-4f57e460d30a.history: Core Qigong practice focusing on the energy center below navel.
def29a93-7f64-459d-af03-4f57e460d30a.safety_warning: Stop if you feel dizzy. Not recommended if you have joint issues.

instructions.instruction: Stand with feet shoulder-width, knees slightly bent.
Begin gently bouncing on your heels.
Let the vibration move through your whole body.
Relax shoulders, jaw, and let arms shake loosely.
Continue for 2 minutes, breathing naturally.
Stop and stand still, feeling the energy flow.

tips: Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable

21c565f5-a70d-41ba-b825-aac9602a6a38.name: Sun Salutation Breath
21c565f5-a70d-41ba-b825-aac9602a6a38.description: Breathing synchronized with saluting the sun. Honoring Tonatiuh (Aztec sun god).
21c565f5-a70d-41ba-b825-aac9602a6a38.history: Combines Aztec sun worship traditions with flowing movement. The sun was considered the source of all life and energy.
21c565f5-a70d-41ba-b825-aac9602a6a38.safety_warning: Move slowly and modify as needed (bend knees in forward folds, keep hands on thighs for support). Stop if you feel dizzy, lightheaded, or have sharp pain. Avoid looking directly at the sun; if outdoors, keep your gaze soft or eyes closed during upward reach.

instructions.instruction: Face the sun (or east in morning).
Stand with hands at heart in prayer position.
Inhale, raising arms overhead, looking up.
Exhale, bowing forward, hands toward earth.
Inhale, rise halfway with flat back.
Exhale, fold. Inhale, rise to standing. Repeat.

tips: Move with breath, not ahead of it

5ed7d346-d542-4437-8f63-0962e6171781.name: Tai Chi Standing
5ed7d346-d542-4437-8f63-0962e6171781.description: Zhan Zhuang - Standing like a tree. A meditation practice for grounding and inner stillness.
5ed7d346-d542-4437-8f63-0962e6171781.history: Zhan Zhuang - Standing like a tree, ancient Taoist practice.
5ed7d346-d542-4437-8f63-0962e6171781.safety_warning: Start with 2-3 minutes and gradually increase. Stop if your legs tremble excessively.

instructions.instruction: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly inward.
Bend knees slightly, as if sitting on a high stool.
Raise your arms as if hugging a large tree in front of you.
Relax your shoulders, letting them drop away from ears.
Breathe naturally, feeling your feet rooted to the ground.
Hold this position, allowing any sensations to arise and pass.

tips: Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable

9b5b173f-34c2-48ab-aa8c-c76c7d8c9f24.name: Vagal Massage
9b5b173f-34c2-48ab-aa8c-c76c7d8c9f24.description: Self-massage technique to stimulate the vagus nerve.
9b5b173f-34c2-48ab-aa8c-c76c7d8c9f24.history: A time-tested breathing technique for wellness.
9b5b173f-34c2-48ab-aa8c-c76c7d8c9f24.safety_warning: Use light pressure only and avoid pressing on the front/side of the neck where you feel a strong pulse (carotid artery). Stop if you feel dizziness, faintness, nausea, or pain. Avoid if you have known carotid artery disease, recent stroke/TIA, or an implanted medical device unless cleared by a clinician.

instructions.instruction: Place two fingers behind your earlobes.
Gently massage in circular motions.
Move down along your neck slowly.
Continue for the duration with gentle pressure.

tips: Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable

ffed1322-8f15-484b-aeff-de1d12b41a4c.name: Walking Meditation
ffed1322-8f15-484b-aeff-de1d12b41a4c.description: Mindful walking synchronized with breath for moving meditation.
ffed1322-8f15-484b-aeff-de1d12b41a4c.history: Buddhist practice found in Zen and Theravada traditions for active mindfulness.
ffed1322-8f15-484b-aeff-de1d12b41a4c.safety_warning: Choose a safe, flat route free of obstacles and avoid doing this while crossing streets or in crowded areas. Stop if you feel dizzy or unsteady, and use support if needed. If you have balance issues, consider practicing near a wall or with a companion.

instructions.instruction: Find a path where you can walk slowly (10-20 steps).
Stand still, take 3 deep breaths.
Begin walking very slowly, feeling each step.
Coordinate: inhale for 2-3 steps, exhale for 2-3 steps.
At the end, turn slowly and walk back.
Continue for 10-15 minutes.

3c3d2624-7dbf-498f-8633-e3ab31606f6d.name: Whirling Breath
3c3d2624-7dbf-498f-8633-e3ab31606f6d.description: Sufi dervish breathing synchronized with turning. Simplified practice without full spinning.
3c3d2624-7dbf-498f-8633-e3ab31606f6d.history: From Mevlevi Sufi order founded by Rumi. Whirling is a form of active meditation seeking divine union.
3c3d2624-7dbf-498f-8633-e3ab31606f6d.safety_warning: Start very slowly. Stop if dizzy. Keep one foot relatively still as pivot.

instructions.instruction: Stand with arms crossed over chest, eyes closed.
Take 3 deep breaths, centering yourself.
Open arms wide, right palm up, left palm down.
Begin turning slowly counterclockwise on the spot.
Breathe naturally, letting go of self.
After 3-5 minutes, slow down and sit in stillness.

91a7b45d-f867-4289-b046-42add7a10f05.name: Body Scan Meditation
91a7b45d-f867-4289-b046-42add7a10f05.description: Systematic attention to body sensations combined with breath awareness.
91a7b45d-f867-4289-b046-42add7a10f05.history: Core MBSR (Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction) practice developed by Jon Kabat-Zinn.
91a7b45d-f867-4289-b046-42add7a10f05.safety_warning: If you feel dizzy, panicky, or emotionally overwhelmed, open your eyes, return attention to the room, and stop. Avoid lying flat if it worsens reflux, breathing issues, or back pain; choose a supported position instead.

instructions.instruction: Lie down comfortably on your back.
Close eyes and take 3 deep breaths.
Bring attention to your feet. Notice sensations.
Slowly move attention up: legs, hips, belly, chest.
Continue to arms, hands, neck, face, head.
If you find tension, breathe into that area.

tips: Don't try to change anything, just notice

e6c3b5ce-95d9-4954-bf51-dc174bb1e11b.name: Cold Exposure
e6c3b5ce-95d9-4954-bf51-dc174bb1e11b.description: Brief cold exposure activates the vagus nerve and builds stress resilience.
e6c3b5ce-95d9-4954-bf51-dc174bb1e11b.history: A time-tested breathing technique for wellness.
e6c3b5ce-95d9-4954-bf51-dc174bb1e11b.safety_warning: Avoid if you have heart conditions, Raynauds disease, or are pregnant. Start gradually and never force yourself.

instructions.instruction: At the end of your regular shower, prepare mentally for cold water.
Take a deep breath and turn the water to cold.
Start with 30 seconds of cold water on your body.
Focus on slow, controlled breathing.
Gradually increase duration over days/weeks up to 2-3 minutes.
End with the cold water and step out feeling invigorated.

tips: Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable

ee6af612-17cd-46e9-a2d8-b309215690cb.name: Ear Massage
ee6af612-17cd-46e9-a2d8-b309215690cb.description: Stimulate vagus nerve branches in the ear through gentle massage.
ee6af612-17cd-46e9-a2d8-b309215690cb.history: A time-tested breathing technique for wellness.
ee6af612-17cd-46e9-a2d8-b309215690cb.safety_warning: Use light pressure only. Stop if you feel pain, dizziness, ringing in the ears, or nausea. Avoid massaging over infection, open skin, recent piercing, or recent ear surgery; seek medical advice if unsure.

instructions.instruction: Sit comfortably and take a few deep breaths.
Gently massage your earlobes between thumb and forefinger.
Move up along the outer edge of your ear, massaging gently.
Press gently into the hollow behind your earlobe.
Massage the inner folds of your ear with light pressure.
Finish by gently pulling your earlobes downward 3 times.

tips: Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable

d635f032-4e3b-4982-9377-38a0412d5825.name: Eye Movement Exercise
d635f032-4e3b-4982-9377-38a0412d5825.description: Gentle eye movements that stimulate the vagus nerve and reduce stress.
d635f032-4e3b-4982-9377-38a0412d5825.history: Based on Stanley Rosenberg's work on the vagus nerve and cranial nerves.
d635f032-4e3b-4982-9377-38a0412d5825.safety_warning: Stop if you feel dizziness, nausea, headache, or eye pain. Avoid if you have a recent concussion, eye surgery, or a condition where eye strain worsens symptoms unless cleared by a clinician.

instructions.instruction: Lie on your back comfortably.
Interlace fingers behind your head.
Without moving your head, look to the right.
Hold for 30-60 seconds until you sigh or yawn.
Return to center, then look left.
Hold again until you sigh, swallow, or yawn.

tips: A sigh or yawn means it's working

f0c841dd-ea2f-4632-9122-317a486d4feb.name: Gargling
f0c841dd-ea2f-4632-9122-317a486d4feb.description: Simple gargling activates muscles connected to the vagus nerve.
f0c841dd-ea2f-4632-9122-317a486d4feb.history: The muscles used in gargling are innervated by the vagus nerve.
f0c841dd-ea2f-4632-9122-317a486d4feb.safety_warning: Do not gargle if you have trouble swallowing or are at risk of choking. Use small sips and stop if you cough, choke, or feel short of breath. Avoid tilting your head far back if it causes dizziness or neck pain.

instructions.instruction: Fill a glass with water.
Take a sip of water.
Tilt head back and gargle vigorously.
Continue until you need to breathe.
Spit out and repeat.
Do this for 1-2 minutes daily.

c79f126e-3bc7-4bca-ba54-6e1db67112fc.name: Grounding Moment
c79f126e-3bc7-4bca-ba54-6e1db67112fc.description: Quick sensory awareness exercise to bring you back to the present.
c79f126e-3bc7-4bca-ba54-6e1db67112fc.history: A time-tested breathing technique for wellness.
c79f126e-3bc7-4bca-ba54-6e1db67112fc.safety_warning: If deep breaths make you lightheaded, switch to normal breathing and do the sensory steps only. If you feel unsafe or overwhelmed, pause and seek support.

instructions.instruction: Notice 5 things you can see.
Notice 4 things you can touch.
Notice 3 things you can hear.
Take 2 deep breaths.
Name 1 thing you are grateful for.

tips: Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable

a03a582d-fc54-4a50-aac4-e2a996cf5ecc.name: Heart 7 - Shen Men
a03a582d-fc54-4a50-aac4-e2a996cf5ecc.description: Acupressure on the "Spirit Gate" point. Calms the heart, reduces anxiety, and promotes peaceful sleep.
a03a582d-fc54-4a50-aac4-e2a996cf5ecc.history: A time-tested breathing technique for wellness.
a03a582d-fc54-4a50-aac4-e2a996cf5ecc.safety_warning: Press gently—do not cause pain, numbness, or tingling. Avoid acupressure over broken/irritated skin or recent wrist injury. Stop if you feel dizzy or unwell.

instructions.instruction: Find the crease on the inside of your wrist.
Locate the point on the pinky side of the crease.
Press gently with thumb, hold for 30 seconds.
Breathe deeply while pressing.
Switch to other wrist and repeat.
Do 3 rounds on each wrist.

tips: Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable

842f8c97-9fea-4c98-9087-02461fe19e8d.name: Humming / OM Chanting
842f8c97-9fea-4c98-9087-02461fe19e8d.description: Vibrations from humming stimulate the vagus nerve through the larynx.
842f8c97-9fea-4c98-9087-02461fe19e8d.history: Bhramari pranayama (bee breath) from Yoga tradition.
842f8c97-9fea-4c98-9087-02461fe19e8d.safety_warning: Keep breathing comfortable—do not strain or force long exhalations. Stop if you feel lightheaded, short of breath, or throat discomfort. If you have asthma/COPD or voice issues, keep it gentle and consult a clinician if symptoms worsen.

instructions.instruction: Sit comfortably with your spine straight.
Take a deep breath in through your nose.
As you exhale, make a humming sound (like mmmmm) or chant OM.
Feel the vibration in your throat, chest, and head.
Continue for the duration, taking natural breaths between hums.
Experiment with different pitches to find what feels most resonant.

tips: The vibration directly stimulates your vagus nerve
Great for anxiety and before sleep

b32a11e9-db86-425e-bc4c-6b00bcd9e241.name: Khoomei Breathing
b32a11e9-db86-425e-bc4c-6b00bcd9e241.description: Mongolian throat singing breathing technique for deep vibration and meditation.
b32a11e9-db86-425e-bc4c-6b00bcd9e241.history: Khoomei (throat singing) has been practiced by Mongolian nomads for centuries. The breathing technique alone is deeply meditative and healing.
b32a11e9-db86-425e-bc4c-6b00bcd9e241.safety_warning: Start gently to avoid straining throat.

instructions.instruction: Sit comfortably with spine straight.
Take a deep breath filling belly completely.
Begin a low drone sound from deep in throat.
Shape mouth to create different overtone harmonics.
Feel vibrations in chest, throat, and head.
Continue for 10-15 minutes, experimenting with sounds.

tips: The sound matters less than the vibration

9b7fa428-6353-4346-b80c-0a4644fc3cf9.name: Military Sleep Method
9b7fa428-6353-4346-b80c-0a4644fc3cf9.description: Technique used by military to fall asleep in 2 minutes or less.
9b7fa428-6353-4346-b80c-0a4644fc3cf9.history: Developed by US Navy Pre-Flight School to help pilots sleep in any conditions.
9b7fa428-6353-4346-b80c-0a4644fc3cf9.safety_warning: If you feel anxious, panicky, or uncomfortable while lying down, switch to a supported position or stop. Do not use this technique while driving or when you need to stay alert.

instructions.instruction: Lie down and relax your entire face, including tongue and jaw.
Drop your shoulders and let arms hang loose.
Exhale and relax your chest.
Relax your legs from thighs down to feet.
Clear your mind for 10 seconds. Think 'don't think'.
Picture yourself in a calm place, or repeat 'don't think'.

tips: Takes 6 weeks of practice to master
Works 96% of the time with practice

ed1ca56a-024b-4e43-a9a5-04f718d90474.name: Pericardium 6 - Nei Guan
ed1ca56a-024b-4e43-a9a5-04f718d90474.description: The "Inner Gate" point relieves nausea, anxiety, and calms the heart. Used for motion sickness too.
ed1ca56a-024b-4e43-a9a5-04f718d90474.history: A time-tested breathing technique for wellness.
ed1ca56a-024b-4e43-a9a5-04f718d90474.safety_warning: Avoid during pregnancy without consulting practitioner.

instructions.instruction: Place 3 fingers above wrist crease on inner arm.
Find the point between the two tendons.
Press firmly but gently with thumb.
Hold for 1 minute while breathing slowly.
Release and repeat on other arm.

tips: Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable

e9cdee6b-70a3-44b7-8e58-e798dc86ab44.name: Progressive Muscle Relaxation
e9cdee6b-70a3-44b7-8e58-e798dc86ab44.description: Systematically tense and release muscle groups to release physical tension.
e9cdee6b-70a3-44b7-8e58-e798dc86ab44.history: Developed by Edmund Jacobson in the 1920s for anxiety and tension relief.
e9cdee6b-70a3-44b7-8e58-e798dc86ab44.safety_warning: Stop if you feel pain, cramping, tingling, or dizziness. Avoid forcefully tensing any injured or recently operated areas; keep contractions gentle and breathe normally.

instructions.instruction: Lie down comfortably. Take 3 deep breaths.
Squeeze your feet tightly for 5 seconds, then release.
Move to calves: squeeze 5 seconds, release.
Continue up: thighs, glutes, belly, chest, hands, arms.
Squeeze face muscles, then release completely.
Finally, tense entire body at once, then let go.

5a59ad55-e2cf-414c-82dd-24e1d7e02b9c.name: Vocal Toning
5a59ad55-e2cf-414c-82dd-24e1d7e02b9c.description: Use your voice to create vibrations that stimulate the vagus nerve.
5a59ad55-e2cf-414c-82dd-24e1d7e02b9c.history: Vocal vibrations have been used across cultures to induce calm and connection.
5a59ad55-e2cf-414c-82dd-24e1d7e02b9c.safety_warning: Keep the volume comfortable and do not strain your voice. Stop if you feel lightheaded, throat pain, or shortness of breath; people with voice/throat conditions should use gentle humming or consult a clinician.

instructions.instruction: Sit or stand comfortably.
Take a deep breath in.
On exhale, make a long 'OOOOMMM' or 'AAAHHH' sound.
Feel the vibration in your chest and throat.
Experiment with different pitches.
Continue for 3-5 minutes.

tips: Lower pitches create stronger chest vibrations

736aba09-ed5d-45d3-b4b9-e42e08a0e1e5.name: Voluntary Yawning
736aba09-ed5d-45d3-b4b9-e42e08a0e1e5.description: Yawning activates the vagus nerve and releases tension in the jaw and face.
736aba09-ed5d-45d3-b4b9-e42e08a0e1e5.history: A time-tested breathing technique for wellness.
736aba09-ed5d-45d3-b4b9-e42e08a0e1e5.safety_warning: Stop if you feel dizzy, lightheaded, or jaw pain. Avoid forcing the jaw wide if you have TMJ symptoms; keep the movement gentle.

instructions.instruction: Sit or lie down comfortably.
Open your mouth wide as if starting a yawn.
Even if you do not feel like yawning, mimic the motion.
Often, a real yawn will follow the fake one.
Allow your body to yawn naturally and fully.
Repeat several times, allowing any sounds or stretches that come naturally.

tips: Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable

090e16d9-5ebc-40e4-816e-8372845c3614.name: Yin Tang - Third Eye
090e16d9-5ebc-40e4-816e-8372845c3614.description: Pressing this point between eyebrows calms the mind and relieves headaches and stress.
090e16d9-5ebc-40e4-816e-8372845c3614.history: A time-tested breathing technique for wellness.
090e16d9-5ebc-40e4-816e-8372845c3614.safety_warning: Use light pressure only and avoid pressing on irritated skin or recent facial injuries. Stop if you feel pain, dizziness, or worsening headache.

instructions.instruction: Find the point between your eyebrows.
Use index finger or thumb to apply gentle pressure.
Close your eyes and breathe slowly.
Hold for 1-2 minutes.
Release slowly and notice the calm.

tips: Stop if you feel dizzy or uncomfortable

706c38f1-ea62-4ce4-9644-8ecd9b1dc456.name: Yoga Nidra
706c38f1-ea62-4ce4-9644-8ecd9b1dc456.description: Yogic sleep - a guided practice between waking and sleeping states.
706c38f1-ea62-4ce4-9644-8ecd9b1dc456.history: Ancient tantric practice systematized by Swami Satyananda Saraswati in the 1960s.
706c38f1-ea62-4ce4-9644-8ecd9b1dc456.safety_warning: Practice in a safe place where you can fully relax (not while driving or operating machinery). If you feel dizzy, anxious, or uncomfortable, open your eyes, take a few normal breaths, and stop.

instructions.instruction: Lie in Savasana (corpse pose) with eyes closed.
Set a Sankalpa (positive intention/resolve).
Rotate awareness through body parts systematically.
Observe breath without changing it.
Visualize peaceful images or scenes.
Return to Sankalpa, then slowly wake up.

tips: One hour equals 4 hours of sleep
